models_evaluated: three widely used LLMs (not named in abstract)

links.outcome: LLM performance disparities across public health topics, including chronic conditions common in older and minority populations
links.effect: Most models scored 13.8% lower than their overall average on topics about chronic conditions occurring in older and minority populations, which the authors interpret as condition-based algorithmic discrimination.
links.quote: Our findings indicate alarming performance disparities across various public health topics, with most of the models exhibiting 13.8% lower performance (compared to an overall average) for all the public health topics that relate to chronic conditions that occur in older and minority populations, which indicates the existence of what's known as condition-based algorithmic discrimination.

unlisted_practices: Component-wise evaluation of medical QA (entity recognition, factual consistency, structured completeness) instead of semantic-similarity metrics alone
Testing whether prompt engineering compensates for entity-extraction limitations in LLMs

screen.reason: Evaluates LLMs across public health topics using a new evaluation framework focusing on safety and health equity, and specifically tests whether prompt engineering compensates for performance failures.
